attributes.residual: TWO separate things remain, and they are independent. (1) THE COUNT DELTA. Retail emits `cmpwi r3,0; bne ->+0x310; b ->+0x1a0` where +0x310 is the IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING instruction -- a branch-to-next, the canonical peephole-off tell. Our build emits the peephole-collapsed `beq ->+0x1a0`. Three distinct C spellings of that conditional all normalise to the identical IR before codegen, so the branch-inversion decision is NOT reachable from goto/if statement spelling in this function. Note the contrast that makes this precise: on update_class_spec, in the SAME run, the one-case switch DID recover the pair -- so the switch lever is real but conditional, and what distinguishes the two sites is that update_class_spec's arms assign a value while these arms are pure control transfers with no value to place. The remaining untried levers are therefore NOT statement respellings: a scoped `#pragma peephole off` around this function (untried here, and hazardous per the recorded rule against unscoped peephole pragmas poisoning downstream functions), or accepting the delta. (2) A SEPARATE WRONG-SYMBOL DEFECT, found while reading the aligned view and NOT probed: at +0x318 retail loads `sFlags`(EMB_SDA21) while we load `gControllerButtons+0x4`(EMB_SDA21). Our `extern s64 gControllerButtons;` (screensaver.c:134) makes `(gControllerButtons & 8)` a 64-bit AND whose low half our object addresses as an addend on gControllerButtons, whereas retail's relocation names the distinct symbol sFlags (declared but unused at screensaver.c:135). Both resolve to the same linked address, so the DOL is correct, but fndiff counts the differing relocation symbol as real. This is a reloc-naming item for a later lane and is orthogonal to the count delta.
